name: Annasäule Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The St. Anne's Column in Innsbruck's Maria-Theresien-Straße: erected 1704–1706 by Cristoforo Benedetti from red Kramsach marble in gratitude for the liberation of the state in 1703.
beschreibung:
Overview

The St. Anne's Column, a magnificent monument in the heart of Innsbruck, is a testament to the deep gratitude of the Tyrolean population. Erected in 1706, it commemorates the withdrawal of Bavarian troops on St. Anne's Day, July 26, 1703, during the War of the Spanish Succession. This Baroque masterpiece, crowned by a statue of Saint Anne, symbolizes the victory and liberation of the city. Its central location on Maria-Theresien-Straße makes it an indispensable part of the historic cityscape and a popular meeting point for locals and visitors alike.

Route & Requirements

St. Anne's Column is located directly on Maria-Theresien-Straße, one of Innsbruck's most famous promenades. It is easily accessible on foot and places no special demands on visitors. Access is barrier-free, so everyone has the opportunity to view this impressive monument up close. There is no specific route to follow; the column is accessible from all sides and serves as an excellent starting point for further exploration of the Old Town. A visit can be ideally combined with a stroll through the surrounding shops and cafés.

Visit & Arrival

St. Anne's Column is a publicly accessible monument and can be visited at any time, free of charge. It is centrally located in the pedestrian zone of Maria-Theresien-Straße. Arrival is straightforward: from Innsbruck main station, the column can be reached in about 10 minutes on foot. Numerous bus and tram lines stop in the immediate vicinity, for example at the "Annasäule/Maria-Theresien-Straße" stop. For drivers, several parking garages are available in the city center, such as the garage at Kaufhaus Tyrol or the Rathausgalerien-Garage, from which the column can also be reached quickly on foot.

Tips

Take your time to admire the details of St. Anne's Column, especially the artistic statues of Saint Anne, Saint Cassian, Saint Vigilius, Saint George, and Saint Roch. A visit in the late afternoon or early evening often offers particularly beautiful light for photos. Combine your visit with a stroll along Maria-Theresien-Straße to admire the magnificent facades of the historic buildings and take a break in one of the many cafés. St. Anne's Column is also an ideal starting point for exploring the Golden Roof and the Hofburg, which are only a few minutes' walk away.
oeffnungszeiten: Freely accessible year-round, 24 hours a day
